A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, core GeoNGNN constructions, and overlapping experiments. All 30 pages of v1 and 39 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Text extraction and visual inspection support matching equations, figures, and tables across the substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic separation experiments, molecular prediction results, symmetry assessments, chirality evaluations, and sampling-policy experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original GeoNGNN and GeoNGNN-C evaluations, revises molecular prediction and symmetry results, and adds original 3BPA generalization results in Appendix F.2.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a general geometric subgraph-GNN family with distance-aware local operations, inter-subgraph aggregation, and alternative pooling schemes (Section 4.2 and Appendix D). It removes v1's node-type sampling and GeoNGNN-P designs. The base DisGNN schematic also replaces paired dense layers with residual blocks. The central GeoNGNN nesting and GeoNGNN-C directed-distance mechanisms remain.

E1.justification: v2 adds 3BPA energy and force prediction, including evaluation at higher temperatures than the training data. This is a targeted extension into temperature-shift scenarios within molecular prediction. Existing synthetic, rMD17, MD22, QM9, ModelNet40, and chirality coverage remains; v1's ModelNet already denotes the same 40-class dataset.

E2.justification: Allegro is removed from the rMD17 comparison in Table 1, although it remains in MD22 and participates in the new 3BPA comparison. The other retained benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. Newly discussed geometric subgraph GNNs are theoretical constructions, not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: For rMD17, reported DisGNN depth changes from 6 to 7 layers and GeoNGNN from (5,1) to (5,2) inner/outer layers; the polynomial envelope changes from p=5 to p=6. The QM9 symmetry assessment now explicitly discards initial labels. The added 3BPA protocol uses a 450/50 training/validation split, 300K training, and RMSE evaluation at 300K, 600K, and 1200K.

E4.justification: v2 removes the extensive node-type and METIS/BRICS partition-sampling analyses, including their negative findings (v1 Appendix E, Tables 6–7). It adds temperature-shift generalization analysis on 3BPA and revises the real-data symmetry assessment. The subgraph-radius sensitivity experiment is retained as v2 Figure 6, rather than newly added.

E5.justification: The new 3BPA table explicitly reports standard deviations over three runs. v1 already includes uncertainty values for chirality results, which remain unchanged, but does not specify this three-run reporting protocol. Neither PDF establishes an increase in repeated runs for the retained experiments.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces DisGNN and GeoNGNN scores: for example, GeoNGNN aspirin energy MAE changes from 0.0490 to 0.0502 and ethanol force MAE from 0.0616 to 0.0482. These accompany changed configurations, and ranks also reflect Allegro's removal. v2 adds 3BPA results, revises symmetry proportions, and removes sampling results. Synthetic separation, MD22, efficiency, and chirality results are retained.

T1.justification: Beyond reformulating existing anchor arguments as C/D-symmetry, v2 adds general subgraph-GNN completeness theorems and proofs, a measure-zero argument, and an O(n^5) complexity derivation including injective-function costs. The earlier O(n^3) accounting excluding those costs remains. The new Proposition B.3 contains an unjustified implication from distinct distance multisets to distinct squared-distance sums, affecting its support for Theorem B.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the contribution from GeoNGNN and three established invariant models to a general family of complete geometric subgraph GNNs under stated conditions. v2 also strengthens the restricted-unidentifiable-space claim to an explicit measure-zero claim and presents expansion of the geometric model design space as a central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds a low-dimensional-distance-graph explanation for the collapse of traditional expressiveness hierarchies. Its 3BPA discussion identifies weaker generalization than MACE, especially under larger temperature shifts, and proposes equivariant representations as a possible remedy. It explicitly cautions that empirical separation does not prove PaiNN/MACE completeness. Interpretations concerning sampling failures disappear with those analyses.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies ModelNet40 downsampling to 256 points, documents 3BPA settings, and adds dataset-specific training times. Hardware reporting changes from RTX 3090/A100 to RTX 4090/A100 with 80GB specified. These improve implementation and resource documentation; the PDFs do not establish whether the newly disclosed downsampling itself changed.

R1.justification: The introduction and expanded Appendix A substantially reposition the work against complete point-cloud invariants, Hordan's near-completeness characterization, 2FWL-based models, and continuous-frame approaches. New references include Widdowson/Kurlin, injective-network theory, and recent frame methods. The relationship to traditional subgraph-GNN hierarchies becomes central, while partition-method references disappear with the sampling appendix.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, and symmetry exposition are extensively rewritten around unlabeled point clouds and C/D-symmetry. Detailed anchor derivations move to the proofs, related work moves to an expanded appendix, and MD22 and subgraph-size discussions move out of the main experimental narrative. Vanilla DisGNN is generally renamed DisGNN, and the appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive display reflow. v2 redraws and combines symmetry illustrations, adds a prior-work set-containment diagram, revises the symmetry plots and architecture schematic, and adds the 3BPA table. The partition schematic and two sampling tables disappear. Several retained figures and tables are relocated or resized.

improvement.justification: v2 adds broader completeness analysis, informative temperature-shift evaluation, and useful computational documentation. However, it removes sampling evidence, and its newly emphasized measure-zero argument relies on Proposition B.3's unjustified inference that distinct distance multisets imply distinct squared-distance sums. These gains coexist with a substantive gap in a new theoretical contribution, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
